title: pen-sim passes when the TV already holds ink, whether or not its stroke landed
body:
## Summary
pen-sim judged PASS on annotationCount > 0, so a TV still holding an earlier drawing passed with the new stroke dropped (tools/pen-sim.mjs:41-47 before the fix).

## Description
The pass predicate read the last state's annotationCount and required it above zero. It never compared against the count before drawing, so the check could not fail on any TV that already had ink - a negative control the check never had (registry test-harness / negative-control-tests). Fixed: the count from the state the TV beats before drawing (heartbeat every 400 ms, PenConversation.kt INTERVAL_MS; pen-sim waits 800 ms) is the baseline, and PASS needs the final count above it; no state before drawing is a FAIL that says so.

## Flow
- a TV holds 3 annotations from an earlier run
- pen-sim draws; the TV drops the stroke
- last state annotationCount = 3 > 0 -> PASS (before) / 3 -> 3 FAIL (after)

## Expected impact
Whoever runs pen-sim on a Stick between live runs gets a FAIL when strokes stop arriving instead of a green line. A TV that never beats state before drawing would now FAIL; the heartbeat makes that impossible today.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - pen-sim FAILs when its own stroke does not arrive
Before: loopback fake TV, count stuck at 3, strokes dropped -> "[pen-sim] PASS" exit 0
After: same fake -> "ink=3->3 FAIL" exit 1; counting fake -> "ink=3->4 PASS" exit 0 (freehand and --shape arrow)
Method: gate - red-then-green on a fake TV over loopback; no device in the round
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Whoever runs pen-sim on a Stick between live runs gets a FAIL when strokes stop arriving instead of a green line. A TV that never beats state before drawing would now FAIL; the heartbeat makes that impossible today.

title: latency-probe crashes with a TypeError instead of FAIL when no probe is answered
body:
## Summary
With zero pongs latency-probe threw "Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toFixed')" at its min line and never printed a verdict (tools/latency-probe.mjs:88-94 before).

## Description
rtts[0] and rtts.at(-1) were formatted unguarded; tail-diag (tools/tail-diag.mjs:40-45) already returns NaN for an empty sample - one rule, two implementations, one fixed. Now pct returns NaN for an empty array, min/max read through it, and ok requires at least one answered probe.

## Flow
- TV paired but never answers ping (wrong build, stuck dispatcher)
- after --seconds the summary formats rtts[0]
- TypeError stack, exit 1 (before) / NaN rows and "FAIL (p95 under 25 ms, no dropped probes)" exit 1 (after)

## Expected impact
The operator reading a hardware run sees the verdict line rather than a stack trace. Exit code unchanged (1).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the probe reports FAIL on an empty sample
Before: fake TV without pongs -> TypeError, no PASS/FAIL line
After: same -> FAIL line, exit 1; answering fake PASS exit 0; 150 ms fake FAIL exit 1
Method: gate - red-then-green on a loopback fake TV
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The operator reading a hardware run sees the verdict line rather than a stack trace. Exit code unchanged (1).

title: tail-diag blames the app when its tcp control leg measured nothing
body:
## Summary
tail-diag dropped failed tcp connects uncounted, so with adbd not on :5555 the control leg had n=0 and every ws stall read "the APP is stalling" (tools/tail-diag.mjs:55-66, 134-142 before).

## Description
The discriminator compares ws stalls with tcp stalls to adbd :5555. A connect error was discarded with no count, and the verdict was printed whenever ws stalled, so an unmeasured control leg (adb over USB, emulator loopback, adb tcpip off) produced a confident app verdict from zero data - the count carried no predicate (registry law count-carries-predicate, failure-not-empty-success). Now failed connects are counted and printed, and with no tcp sample the tool prints "no verdict" and what to check.

## Flow
- run tail-diag against a host where :5555 refuses
- ws stalls recorded, tcp leg n=0
- "0/32 ws stalls coincide with a tcp stall -> the APP is stalling" (before) / "no verdict: the tcp leg connected 0 times (44 failed)" (after)

## Expected impact
The tool that settled the Stick latency tail (docs/POC-FINDINGS.md:222) cannot again point at the app on an empty control. Runs with a working tcp leg print the same verdict as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no app/link verdict from an unmeasured control leg
Before: fake TV pongs at 150 ms, nothing on 127.0.0.1:5555 -> "tcp n=0 ... -> the APP is stalling"
After: same -> "failed tcp connects 44 ... no verdict"; with a listener on :5555 -> tcp n=44 and the verdict as before
Method: gate - red-then-green on a loopback fake TV plus a local listener as control
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
before: tcp (adbd, same Wi-Fi)  n=   0  p50 NaN ...
  0/32 ws stalls coincide with a tcp stall -> the APP is stalling
after: failed tcp connects 44 / no verdict: the tcp leg connected 0 times (44 failed)
impact: The tool that settled the Stick latency tail (docs/POC-FINDINGS.md:222) cannot again point at the app on an empty control. Runs with a working tcp leg print the same verdict as before.

title: live-ui-test leaves the previous run's result file in place when it crashes
body:
## Summary
The crash path exited 3 before writing artifacts/live-ui-test.json, so a green file from an earlier run read as the latest result (tools/live-ui-test.mjs:381-384 before).

## Description
Only the success path wrote the result file; relay-test writes its file in finally on a crash - the pair disagreed. A failure path that skips the record its success path writes is this lens's anchor case. Now the crash path records a failing "live UI test completed" check, adds "crashed", writes the file and still exits 3 (registry test-harness / live-app-harness: a harness failure reported as such).

## Flow
- adb drops mid-run (or a selector times out)
- run() throws -> exit 3
- artifacts/live-ui-test.json still holds yesterday's all-pass body (before) / rewritten with the crash (after)

## Expected impact
Anyone reading artifacts/ after a broken run sees the crash, not a stale pass. No consumer reads the file outside the tool (git grep: 0).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the result file always describes the latest run
Before: stale all-pass file seeded, ADB missing -> exit 3, file unchanged ("when":"2026-10-01")
After: exit 3, file rewritten with ok:false "live UI test completed" and crashed
Method: gate - red-then-green; the run stops at the first adb call before any browser or device
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
run().catch((e) => { console.error('live-ui-test crashed:', e); process.exit(3); }); // no writeFileSync
tools/relay-test.mjs finally { ... writeFileSync(relay-test.json) }
impact: Anyone reading artifacts/ after a broken run sees the crash, not a stale pass. No consumer reads the file outside the tool (git grep: 0).

title: relay-test skips its result file when restoring the LAN transport throws
body:
## Summary
relay-test's finally called restoreLanTransport over adb before writing relay-test.json; with adb failing the throw escaped and the file and summary were skipped (tools/relay-test.mjs:282-293 before).

## Description
The usual reason a device run crashes is adb itself, which is exactly when the restore throws. The uncaught throw ended the process with an unhandled rejection, leaving the previous run's relay-test.json. The restore is now caught and recorded as a failing check.

## Flow
- device drops during relay-test
- catch records "relay test completed" false
- finally: restore throws -> no file, no "n/m checks passed" (before) / failing restore check, file written (after)

## Expected impact
A broken relay run always leaves its own result. Nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the result file survives an adb failure
Before: stale file seeded, ADB missing, spawn stubbed -> uncaught ENOENT, exit 1, file unchanged
After: "0/3 checks passed.", file rewritten with 3 failing checks
Method: gate - red-then-green with a --require preload that stubs child_process.spawn so no relay process starts
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A broken relay run always leaves its own result. Nothing else changes.

title: relay-test exits 1 for a crash where live-ui-test exits 3
body:
## Summary
The two device harnesses disagreed on the crash exit code: live-ui-test 3, relay-test 1, the same code as a failed check (tools/relay-test.mjs:299 before).

## Description
live-app-harness (registry test-harness) asks that a harness failure be reported as such, never as a mere test failure. relay-test now exits 3 after a crash, after writing its file.

## Flow
- relay-test crashes
- exit 1 - indistinguishable from a red check (before) / exit 3 (after)

## Expected impact
A script or reader can tell "the relay path is broken" from "the harness never got there". No caller branches on the code (dev.ps1 does not run relay-test).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - crash vs failed check distinguishable
Before: crash probe exit 1; harnesses agreeing on crash=3: 1 of 2
After: crash probe exit 3; 2 of 2
Method: gate - the same offline crash probe on both sides
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/live-ui-test.mjs: process.exit(3) on crash
tools/relay-test.mjs:299 (before): process.exit(failed.length ? 1 : 0);
impact: A script or reader can tell "the relay path is broken" from "the harness never got there". No caller branches on the code (dev.ps1 does not run relay-test).

title: relay-test's cost note describes only the emulator on a hardware run
body:
## Summary
The note printed beside the relay round-trip said the number is protocol overhead only and that the LAN path goes through an adb tunnel - both false on a Stick (tools/relay-test.mjs:265-269 before).

## Description
Since dev.ps1 -Device and tools/device.mjs, relay-test runs against hardware, where the relay -> TV leg crosses Wi-Fi and nothing is tunnelled. The note now branches on device.mjs IS_TUNNELLED, which had no consumer before.

## Flow
- TV_HOST=10.0.0.142:8765 relay-test
- prints "protocol overhead and nothing else ... adb tunnel" (before) / names the Wi-Fi leg and points at latency-probe (after)

## Expected impact
The operator does not under-read a hardware relay figure as pure overhead. Text only.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the printed explanation matches the path measured
Before: 2 sentences false on the hardware path; IS_TUNNELLED consumers 0
After: 0 false; IS_TUNNELLED consumers 1
Method: probe - the sentences read under both TV_HOST values; the print itself needs a device, so no gate
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/relay-test.mjs (before): 'overhead and nothing else - it will read faster than the LAN path, which goes' / 'through an adb tunnel.'
tools/device.mjs:33 export const IS_TUNNELLED (git grep: no importer)
impact: The operator does not under-read a hardware relay figure as pure overhead. Text only.

title: six harness tools each carry their own copy of the argv parser
body:
## Summary
live-ui-test, relay-test, relay-stub, pen-sim, latency-probe and tail-diag each inlined the same Object.fromEntries(process.argv...) parser.

## Description
Six copies of one rule. It is now parseArgs() in tools/device.mjs with identical semantics; device-rules-test pins the parser and that no tool parses argv itself (97381dd8).

## Flow
- add parseArgs to device.mjs
- replace the six copies
- pin with a source scan in tools/device-rules-test.cjs

## Expected impact
A future flag rule changes in one place. relay-stub now imports device.mjs (built-ins only).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one parser
Before: 6 inline copies
After: 1 (device.mjs), 6 importers
Method: gate - grep count plus offline probes of every tool on the change
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: grep "flatMap((a, i, all)" tools/*.mjs -> live-ui-test, relay-test, relay-stub, pen-sim, latency-probe, tail-diag (before); device.mjs only (after)
impact: A future flag rule changes in one place. relay-stub now imports device.mjs (built-ins only).

title: the harness's shared helpers in device.mjs had no test
body:
## Summary
pinFromLogcat, pairingPin, hostAddressForDevice and the argv parser decide every device run before it reaches the device, and no suite covered them.

## Description
The PIN reader was proven once by an uncommitted probe (942925d9). tools/device-rules-test.cjs (built-ins only, wired into desk/package.json rulesSuites before harness-rules-test) pins the last pairing line, ?pin=/&pin=, --pin without adb, the logcat arguments, the emulator alias, the subnet pick over a virtual switch, TV_RELAY_HOST, the no-address sentence and parseArgs. hostAddressForDevice takes its interface list as an optional argument.

## Flow
- write the suite
- seed: pinFromLogcat takes the first line, pen-sim parses argv inline -> 2 red
- restore -> green

## Expected impact
A regression in PIN or address selection is caught by npm test without a Stick. Coupled: desk/package.json (one line).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - offline coverage of the device helpers
Before: 0 tests over device.mjs
After: 9 tests (now 11 with the README and PHONE cases), all green; seeded 2 red
Method: gate - red-then-green on seeded violations
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
git grep "device.mjs" tools/*-test.cjs -> no hit (before)
run-rules --list [device-rules-test.cjs]: green 9/9
impact: A regression in PIN or address selection is caught by npm test without a Stick. Coupled: desk/package.json (one line).

title: README's harness check counts drifted twice in a row
body:
## Summary
README said live-ui-test makes 28 checks and relay-test 11; a full run makes 29 and 13, and the row omitted tail-diag and device.mjs (README.md:52 before).

## Description
605b0f9b added a live-ui-test check in a commit that edited README and left the count; 3b2ac640 added two relay checks without touching it. A hand-maintained figure with no derivation (SKILL 4.7). A device-rules-test case now derives each figure from the check() calls a full run makes and fails on disagreement.

## Flow
- count check() calls less failure-only ones
- compare with README's tools row
- fix the row

## Expected impact
The next check added without a README edit goes red in npm test. Coupled: README.md, one row.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the doc's counts match the code
Before: 2 of 2 counts stale (28 vs 29, 11 vs 13); case red
After: 0 stale; case green; seeded 12 -> red
Method: gate - red-then-green
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
README.md:52 "pixel assertions, 28 checks" / "no listening socket, 11 checks"
AssertionError: README says 28 checks for live-ui-test.mjs; a full run makes 29
impact: The next check added without a README edit goes red in npm test. Coupled: README.md, one row.

title: dev.ps1's boot stage could wait forever with nothing on screen
body:
## Summary
The boot stage used `adb wait-for-device` (2 sites) and an unbounded boot_completed loop (scripts/dev.ps1:248, 259-260 before).

## Description
A missing AVD or an emulator that dies at start, and a Stick still showing its "Allow USB debugging?" prompt (unauthorized is never "device"), hung the cycle silently. Wait-Device polls getprop sys.boot_completed (fails fast with no device) with a 300 s / 60 s deadline and throws with adb's answer and a hint (registry test-harness / platform-quirk-absorption: silence becomes a named diagnosis).

## Flow
- ./scripts/dev.ps1 -Avd typo
- emulator.exe exits; the loop polls forever (before) / throws after 300 s naming -list-avds (after)

## Expected impact
The operator gets a sentence instead of a hung terminal. A booted device returns as before.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every boot wait is bounded
Before: probe: the loop extracted from the AST with Adb stubbed to "no devices" still waiting after 15 s (killed); wait-for-device sites 2
After: Wait-Device -TimeoutSec 3 throws after 4.2 s; stub answering 1 returns in 0.01 s; sites 0
Method: gate - offline unit over the parsed script with a stubbed Adb; the real boot stage needs an emulator
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
scripts/dev.ps1 (before): (Adb wait-for-device) | Out-Null
      while ((Adb shell getprop sys.boot_completed).Output -ne '1') { Start-Sleep -Seconds 2 }
impact: The operator gets a sentence instead of a hung terminal. A booted device returns as before.

title: relay-test drove the companion as a different phone than live-ui-test
body:
## Summary
relay-test opened the companion at deviceScaleFactor 2 with the default HeadlessChrome UA; live-ui-test as a Pixel 8 at 2.625 with an Android UA (tools/relay-test.mjs:190-195, tools/live-ui-test.mjs:80-87 before).

## Description
The relay test claims the same phone over another transport, but the companion sizes its canvases by devicePixelRatio (companion/index.html:313-315). device.mjs now exports one PHONE profile and both tools use it; a device-rules-test case pins that neither sets its own.

## Flow
- add PHONE to device.mjs
- both tools call browser.newContext(PHONE)
- pin with a source case

## Expected impact
The relay path is exercised on the same canvas size as the LAN path. relay-test now runs at DPR 2.625 (touch is dispatched in CSS px, TV pixel thresholds unaffected).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one phone across both transports
Before: 2 profiles differing in 2 fields; case red
After: 1 profile, 2 of 2 tools; case green; chromium probe DPR 2.625 + Pixel 8 UA
Method: gate - red-then-green plus a local headless-chromium probe
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/relay-test.mjs (before): deviceScaleFactor: 2, (no userAgent)
tools/live-ui-test.mjs (before): deviceScaleFactor: 2.625, userAgent: ...Pixel 8...
impact: The relay path is exercised on the same canvas size as the LAN path. relay-test now runs at DPR 2.625 (touch is dispatched in CSS px, TV pixel thresholds unaffected).

title: dev.ps1's live stage ignores npm install failure and never installs Chromium
body:
## Summary
The live stage installs tools/node_modules only when the folder is missing, pipes npm to Out-Null without checking $LASTEXITCODE, and never runs `npx playwright install chromium` (scripts/dev.ps1:168).

## Description
On a fresh machine or after a playwright bump the run fails inside live-ui-test with chromium.launch "Executable doesn't exist", reported only as "live UI test failed". A failed npm install is invisible, and a node_modules folder that predates a new dependency is never refreshed. Fix: check npm's exit code, install when package-lock.json is newer than node_modules, and run `npx playwright install chromium` once (registry test-harness / platform-quirk-absorption).

## Flow
- fresh clone, ./scripts/dev.ps1 -Stage live
- npm install output discarded
- live-ui-test exits 3 at chromium.launch
- dev.ps1 throws "live UI test failed"

## Expected impact
A new machine or a playwright bump fails with a named step instead of a crash inside the test. The install step touches the network; it is the operator's run.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - setup failures named at the setup step
Before: npm install exit code unchecked (dev.ps1:168); browser install steps 0
After: npm exit code checked; 1 browser install step
Method: simulation - needs npm and a browser download; not reachable offline in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: scripts/dev.ps1:168  if (-not (Test-Path node_modules)) { npm install --no-audit --no-fund | Out-Null }
impact: A new machine or a playwright bump fails with a named step instead of a crash inside the test. The install step touches the network; it is the operator's run.
instrument: Run `./scripts/dev.ps1 -Stage live` in a fresh clone with tools/node_modules absent and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointed at an empty temp dir (stub the device with TV_HOST at a dead port): Before = the run fails inside live-ui-test ("Executable doesn't exist" or a missing package) with "live UI test failed"; After = it stops at the install step with npm's exit code, or installs chromium and proceeds to the first device call.

title: the relay stub never tells the phone the TV left
body:
## Summary
When the TV's socket closes, relay-stub clears it but leaves the phone's socket open and drops the phone's frames to the absent peer silently (tools/relay-stub.mjs:102, 106-111).

## Description
After a TV app restart on the relay transport, the phone shows paired, every stroke goes nowhere, and the new TV session (new PIN, Session.kt:78) has no pen. The companion only re-pairs when its own socket closes. relay-test 5b covers the mirror case (the TV is never told a phone left). The stub is the stand-in for the production relay (API Gateway + Lambda), so the rule belongs in the relay contract as well.

## Flow
- phone paired through the relay
- TV app restarts (crash, update, relaunch)
- phone keeps drawing into a socket whose peer is gone; no error frame, no close

## Expected impact
A viewer whose TV restarted sees "reconnecting" and re-pairs instead of drawing into nothing. Could break: a phone briefly disconnected during a TV reconnect race.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the phone learns the TV is gone
Before: pen frames to an absent TV dropped with no trace: 1 path
After: 0 silent paths
Method: simulation - needs a running relay stub, which this round was not allowed to start
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/relay-stub.mjs:102  if (other && other.readyState === other.OPEN) other.send(text);
tools/relay-stub.mjs:106-111 on tv close: tv = null; lastState = null; (pen left open)
impact: A viewer whose TV restarted sees "reconnecting" and re-pairs instead of drawing into nothing. Could break: a phone briefly disconnected during a TV reconnect race.
instrument: An offline relay-stub test with two ws clients on loopback: TV connects, pen connects, TV closes, pen sends a stroke. Before: the pen socket stays open and the stroke vanishes with no frame or close. After: the pen socket is closed (e.g. 1012) so the companion's 1 s reconnect (companion/index.html:177-185) re-hellos once the TV is back.

title: any LAN client can dial the relay as the TV and receive the phone's PIN
body:
## Summary
relay-stub listens on 0.0.0.0, gives the TV slot to whoever upgrades at /tv (closing the real TV), and ignores the session id RelayTransport documents (tools/relay-stub.mjs:76-82, 122; tv-app/src/main/kotlin/dev/telestrator/tv/transport/RelayTransport.kt:28-32).

## Description
RelayTransport says the relay "pairs one TV with one phone by session id" (wss://relay/tv?session=abc, phone at /?session=abc). The stub has one global TV slot and one pen slot. A second /tv dialer replaces the TV and is forwarded the phone's hello - PIN included - and every stroke. The PIN check stays on the TV by design, so the relay is exactly where TV identity must be decided, and nothing decides it. Fixing the stub alone is easy; the decision is the production relay's contract (session ids, who may claim the TV side), which is architecture.

## Flow
- relay-test (or a dev) runs the stub on 0.0.0.0:9787
- a LAN host connects ws://<host>:9787/tv
- the real TV is closed; the impostor receives the phone's {"type":"hello","pin":...}

## Expected impact
Today a dev-time exposure on the LAN; for the hosted relay it decides whether a stranger can take over a living-room session. Escalated: the relay contract is a product architecture call (docs/PLATFORM-RISK.md).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - the relay binds a TV side to one session
Before: TV identity checks in the stub: 0; session id honoured: no
After: not built - needs the contract decision
Method: simulation - architecture escalation; a stub-only patch would not settle the production relay
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: architecture
impact: Today a dev-time exposure on the LAN; for the hosted relay it decides whether a stranger can take over a living-room session. Escalated: the relay contract is a product architecture call (docs/PLATFORM-RISK.md).

title: the TV pixel classifier and capture are copied in live-ui-test and relay-test
body:
## Summary
tvScreenshot, the yellow ink predicate and countInk exist twice (tools/live-ui-test.mjs:29-60, tools/relay-test.mjs:42-61) and have already drifted at the bottom-band boundary.

## Description
live-ui-test skips rows y > 0.94h; relay-test loops y < 0.94h, so the boundary row counts in one and not the other. Any change to the ink colour, the pairing-card mask or the status-bar band has to be made twice. Move them to one module (device.mjs, or a new screen helper - a new file needs a context-map entry), with a pure countInk({width,height,data}) testable offline.

## Flow
- extract countInk/INK/tvScreenshot
- both tools import them
- pin with a synthetic frame in device-rules-test

## Expected impact
One pixel rule for both device journeys. Could break: thresholds tuned to one loop form (difference is one row).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one pixel classifier
Before: 2 copies, 1 boundary disagreement
After: 1 copy, 0
Method: simulation - pure refactor of device-only code; the synthetic-frame instrument is unbuilt
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/relay-test.mjs:52  for (let y = 0; y < height * 0.94; y++)
tools/live-ui-test.mjs:51-52  for (let y = 0; y < height; y++) { if (y > height * 0.94) continue;
impact: One pixel rule for both device journeys. Could break: thresholds tuned to one loop form (difference is one row).
instrument: A device-rules-test case that feeds one synthetic RGBA frame (ink on row floor(0.94*h), ink inside the pairing-card mask, ink elsewhere) to the shared countInk and to each tool's copy; Before = the two copies disagree by the boundary row; After = one function, one count.
